CHILDCARE ENROLLMENT MIX OPTIMIZER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Which children should I enrol to make the most from my space?

Enter your usable floor space, what a teacher costs, and for each age group the tuition, the licensing ratio and group size, the space each child needs and how many families want a place. The tool checks every possible enrolment mix and shows the one with the highest weekly profit, where each extra teacher is triggered, and what the usual fill-the-expensive-room-first approach leaves behind.

Arithmetic on figures you type. Not licensing, financial or tax advice. The example figures are placeholders, not any centre's tuition or wages, and not any state's rules.

Questions owners ask

How many children should a childcare center enrol in each age group?

It depends on your floor space, the ratios you must staff to, tuition by age and how many families want a place. Infant rooms charge the most but need a teacher for every few children and the most space, so filling them first is often not the most profitable plan. This tool checks every combination of enrolment across your age groups and shows the one with the highest weekly profit that fits the space.

Why does one more child sometimes lose money?

Staffing is a staircase. If a room is exactly at its ratio, the next child needs another teacher on the floor, and one child's tuition rarely covers a teacher. The results show, for each age group, what the next child adds or costs and how many places remain before the next hire.

What do I enter for staff-to-child ratio and group size?

The limits your state licensing agency sets for each age group, or tighter ones you choose to staff to. Rules differ by state and change; this tool does not look them up. Check them with your licensing office.

What cost per teacher hour should I use?

Hourly wage plus employer payroll taxes, workers' compensation and any benefits. The coverage factor multiplies teacher hours to cover breaks, planning time and absences, so 1.15 means 15 percent extra paid hours beyond the hours you are open.

Does it tell me what more space or a stricter ratio rule would do?

Yes. It reports the next amount of extra floor space that would raise weekly profit, and re-solves with every ratio one child tighter and with wages 10 percent higher so you can see how exposed the plan is.

Is this financial or licensing advice?

No. It is arithmetic on figures you type. It does not know your licensing rules, subsidy contracts, enrolment timing or payroll law, and it does not replace your licensing office or an accountant.

Not decided

Your state's actual ratios and space rules, mixed-age rooms and ratio blending, part-time and drop-in enrolment, subsidy rates and payment delays, enrolment timing and turnover, a director or cook who counts toward ratio, and which children you can actually find. Every figure is treated as a steady weekly average, and teachers are assumed to be hired in whole numbers.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, or financial advice. Results are arithmetic on figures you type; verify with your licensing office and a qualified professional before you rely on them.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, report_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Already know your enrolment? The childcare center break-even calculator shows break-even enrollment and ratio cliffs, and the childcare tuition calculator works the per-family side.
